summary: Port reproduces the string-light structure exactly — same bulb pitch, same 5-colour repeating sequence, same one-frame twinkle blackout — but two of the five hues are visibly shifted, the bulb halo is ~2.4x brighter, and the twinkle fires ~5x too often at 20 fps because the port's rate is time-based where the original's is frame-based.
observations: Both sides draw a static string of single-pixel 'bulbs' at a fixed 18-px pitch starting at index 1 (60-px strip: bulbs at px 1, 19, 37, 55). Pitch is independent of strip length on BOTH sides — a --pixels 120 run put bulbs at 1,19,37,55,73,91,109 on both, and a 16x16 grid re-render (--rig grid --grid 16x16) gave both sides the same 15-bulb diagonal at indices 1,19,...,253.

Each bulb has a halo of exactly ±1 pixel and nothing at ±2, on both sides. Halo intensity differs: original halo is 6.3% of the bulb value (bulb 254,0,7 -> neighbours 16,0,0); port halo is 14.9% (bulb 255,0,0 -> neighbours 38,0,0). Port's glow is ~2.4x brighter, which shows up as mean brightness 8 vs 7 across every window measured.

Palette is a fixed, seed-independent 5-colour cycle in the SAME order on both sides (red, blue, green, orange, purple, repeat). Verified identical at seeds 1, 7 and 1234 — colours never vary with seed, so the hue differences below are real, not RNG.

Exact palette RGB (--dump, 60-px default rig, t=0). slot0 red: orig 254,0,7 (hue 358) vs port 255,0,0 (hue 0) — match. slot1 blue: orig 0,102,254 (hue ~196, a cyan/azure sky-blue) vs port 0,10,255 (hue ~238, deep blue) — ~42 deg apart, clearly different on screen. slot2 green: orig 0,254,25 (hue ~126) vs port 5,255,0 (hue ~119) — match. slot3 orange: orig 254,30,0 (hue ~7, reads as red-orange, nearly indistinguishable from slot0 red) vs port 255,137,0 (hue ~32, a clear amber orange) — ~25 deg apart and visibly different. slot4 purple: orig 158,0,254 (hue ~277) vs port 188,0,255 (hue ~284) — match.

The ONLY animation on either side is a twinkle: one lit pixel (bulb centre or halo pixel) drops to exactly (0,0,0) for exactly one frame, then restores. Verified by dumping all 600 frames of a 30 s / 20 fps window: the original had 2 such events (px36 at t=3.05, px18 at t=11.85), the port had 36, and in every case exactly one pixel changed and only for one frame. Mechanism and appearance are identical; only the rate differs.

Twinkle rate is frame-rate-coupled on the ORIGINAL and time-coupled on the PORT. Counting motionLit events over a 120 s window at three rates: original 8 events at 10 fps (0.067/s), 23 at 20 fps (0.19/s), 49 at 40 fps (0.41/s) — i.e. ~constant per frame (~1/100 frames), doubling per second as fps doubles. Port: 110 at 10 fps (0.92/s), 120 at 20 fps (1.00/s), 132 at 40 fps (1.10/s) — ~constant per second. At the harness default 20 fps the port twinkles ~5x more often than the original.

No mode rotation, no drift, no warm-up on either side. A 60 s / 5 fps survey, a 120 s / 20 fps run and a --skip 180 --seconds 20 late window all show the same single regime; bulb colours dumped at t=180, 190 and 199.9 s are byte-identical to t=0 on both sides, and brightnessTrend is 'steady' for both everywhere.
Neither side has any controls (both control lists empty in meta.json; --probe-controls reported '(no settable controls)' for both) — control surfaces match.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), no compile or runtime errors on any run.
feedback: Twinkle rate is the pattern's only motion and the port's is ~5x too fast at 20 fps: original produces ~0.19 blank-pixel events/second at 20 fps (about one visible twinkle every 5 s on a 60-px strip), port produces ~1.0/second. Slow the twinkle probability by roughly 5x at 20 fps.

Related and probably the same bug: the original's twinkle probability is evaluated PER FRAME (measured 0.067, 0.19, 0.41 events/s at 10, 20, 40 fps — doubling with fps), while the port's is per SECOND (0.92, 1.00, 1.10 events/s at the same three rates). Matching the original means making the chance-of-twinkle a fixed per-frame probability rather than scaling it by elapsed time.

Palette slot 3 (the 4th bulb, at px 55 on a 60-px strip) is too orange: original is 254,30,0 — a red-orange that reads almost as a second red — while the port renders 255,137,0, a distinctly amber orange. Pull that hue back toward red by about 25 degrees.

Palette slot 1 (the 2nd bulb, px 19) is too deep a blue: original is 0,102,254, a cyan-leaning azure with a strong green component; port is 0,10,255, an almost pure blue. Raise the green component so the hue lands near 196 degrees instead of 238.

The per-bulb halo is too bright: original lights the two neighbour pixels at 6.3% of the bulb value (254 -> 16), port at 14.9% (255 -> 38). Cut the neighbour falloff to roughly 1/16 of the bulb instead of ~1/7; the ±1-pixel extent itself is correct.

Everything else already matches and should not be touched: 18-px bulb pitch starting at index 1 (fixed pitch, independent of strip length), the 5-colour repeating sequence and its order, the red/green/purple hues, the single-pixel one-frame full-blackout twinkle mechanism, and the complete absence of any other animation or controls.
